## Intro:

- In R functions are quite straightforward. Imagine we have a data frame with variable that we wish to perform some arrgregates on, and for simplicity let's use the `gss` data from `forcats`:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
gss <- forcats::gss_cat
# readr::write_csv(gss, "Data/R4DS/gss.csv")
```

- Imagine now we want to perform some operations on this data in order to generate an output file. For that, we need a `data frame function`, i.e., a function that takes a data frame as input and produces a data frame as output:

```{r}
prop_data <- function(df, var) {
  # Set label using rlang:
  lbs <- rlang::as_label(enquo(var)) |>
    str_to_title() |>
    str_replace_all("_", " ")

  # Data frame function
  data <- df |>
    mutate({{ var }} := forcats::as_factor({{ var }})) |>
    count({{ var }}, .drop = FALSE) |>
    mutate(
        prop = n / sum(n),
        prop_pct = (n / sum(n)) |> scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1),
        is_na = if_else({{ var }} %in% c("No answer"), "Yes", "No"),
        n_valid = if_else(is_na == "Yes", NA_real_, n),
        prop_valid = if_else(is_na == "Yes", NA_real_, n_valid / sum(n_valid, na.rm = TRUE)),
        prop_valid_pct = if_else(is_na == "Yes", NA_real_, (n_valid / sum(n_valid, na.rm = TRUE))) |> scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1),
        n_tot = sum(n),
        n_tot_valid = sum(n_valid, na.rm = TRUE),
        n_na = if_else(is_na == "Yes", n, NA_real_),
        na_prop = if_else(is_na == "Yes", n_na / sum(n), NA_real_),
        na_prop_pct = if_else(is_na == "Yes", n_na / sum(n), NA_real_) |> scales::percent(accuracy = 0.1))

  # Use cli to showcase:
  cli::cli_h1("data: {lbs}")
  print(data)

  # Plot:
  cli::cli_h1("Plot: {lbs}")
  p <- data |> 
    ggplot(aes(x = prop, y = {{ var }})) + 
    geom_col()
  print(p)

  # return data quietly:
  invisible(list(data = data, label = lbs, plot = p))
}
t <- gss |> prop_data(marital)
```

- This setup above could be thought of as a 'God-function',
